docs.title: 🛒 Grocery Helper
docs.text: A Python library, command-line interface, and Streamlit application that integrates with AnyList to find optimal grocery pricing across stores.

docs.title: What is Grocery Helper?
docs.text:
Most shoppers create a grocery list in AnyList and then wonder:

"Where should I buy these groceries to save the most money, and is it worth visiting multiple stores?"

Grocery Helper answers this question by: 1. Importing your grocery lists from AnyList (or using built-in demo lists). 2. Fetching real-time and regional prices across major grocers (ALDI, Trader Joe's, Kroger, and Whole Foods). 3. Analyzing the trade-offs: - Split Basket: Cheapest overall price by buying each item at its cheapest store. - Single Store: The best single store if you only want to make one stop. - Constrained Stops: Limit your route to at most $N$ stores (e.g. at most 2 stops). 4. Exporting store-specific sub-lists back into AnyList with one click!

docs.title: grocery_helper.models
docs.text: Defines the core domain entities: - GroceryItem: Product identifier, display name, quantity, measurement unit, category, and checked status. - GroceryList: List container with creation and modification timestamps. - StorePrice: Pricing data per store including regular and promotional sale price. - PriceComparison: Cross-store price matrix for a single item. - OptimizedCart: The output of basket optimization, including item-to-store mappings, total basket cost, potential savings, and single-store comparison totals.

docs.title: grocery_helper.anylist_client
docs.text: Async HTTP client designed around AnyList's reverse-engineered /data/ endpoints: - Generates required X-AnyLeaf-API-Version: 3 and device UUID X-AnyLeaf-Client-Identifier headers. - Handles user authentication, session token retention, and shopping list CRUD. - Seamless fallback to demo_mode with sample lists ("Weekly Shop", "Party Supplies", "Brunch & Coffee"). - export_split_lists() generates store-specific sub-lists back in AnyList.

docs.title: grocery_helper.pricing
docs.text:
• BasePricingProvider: Protocol specifying async def get_prices(item, store_zip) -> list[StorePrice].
  • MockPricingProvider: Generates deterministic prices with store price profiles (ALDI, Trader Joe's, Kroger, Whole Foods) based on catalog matching or name hashes.
  • KrogerPricingProvider: Authenticates with Kroger Developer OAuth2, resolves nearest store location by ZIP code, and retrieves live SKU prices.
  • PricingService:
  • In-memory TTL caching with cache keys formatted as cache_key(item.name, zip).
  • Overlays live Kroger prices onto regional store matrices.
  • Computes unconstrained split basket and evaluates max_stores combinations using subset cover analysis.

docs.title: grocery_helper.matcher
docs.text: Normalizes AnyList user inputs: - Regex-based quantity and unit parser (e.g. "Honeycrisp Apples 3 lbs" $\to$ 3.0, Unit.LB). - Token overlap and sequence matching score calculation.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.
Initial release of Grocery Helper — a Python library, CLI, and Streamlit application that connects to AnyList, compares grocery prices across stores, and computes optimal shopping routes.

docs.title: Core & Architecture
docs.text:
• Data Models (grocery_helper.models):
  • GroceryItem: ID, name, quantity, unit, category, notes, and checked status.
  • GroceryList: Container with timestamps and list metadata.
  • StorePrice: Price per unit, sale price, store identifiers, and effective price computation.
  • PriceComparison: Multi-store item comparison, identifying cheapest grocer and potential savings.
  • OptimizedCart: Multi-store split assignments, total basket cost, estimated savings, single-store comparison totals, and route constraint metadata.
  • Centralized Configuration (grocery_helper.config):
  • Pydantic Settings integration reading environment variables and .env files.
  • Settings for AnyList credentials, Kroger Developer API credentials, cache TTL, and default ZIP code.
  • Shared Utilities (grocery_helper.utils):
  • Normalized in-memory TTL caching (TTLCache) for price queries.
  • Currency and savings string formatters (format_currency, format_savings).
  • @timed execution profiling decorator for sync and async functions.

docs.title: AnyList Integration (grocery_helper.anylist_client)
docs.text:
• Async HTTP client with internal AnyList API endpoints (/data/users/login, /data/shopping-lists/get, /data/shopping-lists/add-item, etc.).
  • Mobile client header support (X-AnyLeaf-API-Version: 3, X-AnyLeaf-Client-Identifier, custom User-Agent).
  • Offline Demo Mode:
  • Provides pre-populated sample lists ("Weekly Shop", "Party Supplies", "Brunch & Coffee").
  • Enables zero-configuration testing and local UI preview without active AnyList credentials.
  • Sub-List Export:
  • export_split_lists() method to generate store-specific shopping lists (e.g. "Weekly Shop (ALDI)", "Weekly Shop (Kroger)") directly in AnyList.

docs.title: Pricing & Basket Optimization (grocery_helper.pricing)
docs.text:
• Pluggable Provider Protocol (BasePricingProvider):
  • Standardized interface for querying grocery item pricing by location.
  • Mock Pricing Provider (MockPricingProvider):
  • Generates realistic, deterministic pricing profiles for ALDI, Trader Joe's, Kroger, and Whole Foods.
  • Handles regular price variations and occasional promotional sale discounts.
  • Live Kroger Developer API Provider (KrogerPricingProvider):
  • OAuth2 client credentials authentication against api.kroger.com.
  • Automatic nearest store location discovery using ZIP code.
  • Live product search and real-time regular and promotional price extraction.
  • Optimization Algorithms:
  • Unconstrained multi-store split optimization for maximum savings.
  • Constrained Route Optimization:
    • allowed_stores: Restrict shopping exclusively to selected stores.
    • max_stores: Limit stops to at most $N$ stores (e.g. max_stores=1 for single-trip shopping, max_stores=2 for two-store split).
  • Single-store basket totals comparison to weigh travel inconvenience against multi-store savings.

docs.title: Item Normalization & Matching (grocery_helper.matcher)
docs.text:
• Regex-based embedded quantity and unit extractor (e.g. "Honeycrisp Apples 3 lbs" $\to$ 3.0, LB).
  • Text normalizer stripping punctuation, abbreviations, and case variations.
  • Token-overlap and sequence-matching similarity scoring to match user item names to store SKUs.

docs.title: User Interfaces
docs.text:
• Streamlit Web Application (grocery_helper.app):
  • Interactive sidebar with credential configuration, ZIP code lookup, and demo mode toggle.
  • Optimization controls: Allowed stores multiselect and max stores trip limit slider.
  • In-app "➕ Add Item" form to append items to lists directly in the web UI.
  • Comprehensive price comparison data table with sale indicators and best store badges.
  • Metrics cards (Optimized Total, Estimated Savings, Best Single Store recommendation).
  • Total basket cost comparison bar chart (st.bar_chart).
  • Expandable shopping route per store with subtotal breakdowns.
  • One-click "📤 Export Store Lists to AnyList" button.
  • CLI Interface (grocery_helper.cli):
  • grocery-helper serve: Launches Streamlit application with configurable --port and --host.
  • grocery-helper optimise <list_id>: Headless CLI optimization with --demo, --zip, --max-stores, --stores, and --json export flags.

docs.title: CI/CD & Testing
docs.text:
• GitHub Actions CI workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml) testing formatting, linting, type-checking, and coverage on push and pull requests.
  • Test suite with 100 tests spanning unit tests, model tests, mock HTTP transport tests, and Streamlit AppTest UI flow tests.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• Non-Developer Shopper's Guide: Comprehensive, step-by-step user guide explaining the app workflow, store selection, "max stores" trip slider, AnyList sub-list export, and item naming tips for everyday shoppers.
  • GitHub Pages Documentation Site: MkDocs Material site deployed automatically via GitHub Actions (.github/workflows/docs.yml) covering architecture, Streamlit UI, CLI reference, configuration, and developer setup.

docs.title: ⚙️ Configuration Reference
docs.text: Grocery Helper manages its configuration using pydantic-settings, reading from environment variables and .env files.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Type Default Description ANYLIST_EMAIL String "" AnyList account login email. ANYLIST_PASSWORD String "" AnyList account login password. ANYLIST_API_BASE_URL String https://www.anylist.com Base URL for AnyList internal API routes. DEFAULT_STORE_ZIP String "" Default ZIP code for grocery store lookups. PRICE_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS Integer 3600 In-memory price result caching duration in seconds. KROGER_CLIENT_ID String "" OAuth2 Client ID from Kroger Developer Portal. KROGER_CLIENT_SECRET String "" OAuth2 Client Secret from Kroger Developer Portal. KROGER_API_BASE_URL String https://api.kroger.com/v1 Base URL for Kroger Developer API. APP_TITLE String Grocery Helper Title displayed in Streamlit browser tabs. DEBUG Boolean false Enable verbose debug logging output.

docs.title: Kroger Developer API Setup (Optional)
docs.text:
To enable live grocery prices from Kroger: 1. Register for a free developer account at developer.kroger.com. 2. Create a new App in your Kroger developer dashboard. 3. Copy your Client ID and Client Secret. 4. Add them to your .env file: 

KROGER_CLIENT_ID=your_client_id_here
KROGER_CLIENT_SECRET=your_client_secret_here
5. When running optimizations, live Kroger SKU prices will automatically overlay onto your results!

docs.title: Building the Documentation Locally
docs.text:
To preview the documentation site locally with hot-reloading:

uv run mkdocs serve

Then visit http://127.0.0.1:8000 in your browser.

To build the static HTML site for publishing:

The compiled static assets will be located in the site/ directory.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• uv (Fast Python package and environment manager)
  • Python 3.11+

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Clone the repository and install dependencies with uv:

git clone https://github.com/cuyler/grocery_helper.git
cd grocery_helper

# Install dependencies into virtualenv managed by uv
uv sync

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Copy the example environment template:

cp .env.example .env

Open .env in your editor:

# ── AnyList credentials (Optional for Demo Mode) ───────────────────────────
ANYLIST_EMAIL=you@example.com
ANYLIST_PASSWORD=your_password

# ── Store settings ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DEFAULT_STORE_ZIP=90210

# ── Cache ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PRICE_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS=3600

# ── Kroger Developer API (Optional live data) ─────────────────────────────────
KROGER_CLIENT_ID=
KROGER_CLIENT_SECRET=

Demo Mode Works Out of the Box

If you don't provide AnyList credentials or Kroger API keys, Grocery Helper automatically runs in Demo Mode. You can immediately explore sample grocery lists and mock pricing without creating any accounts.

docs.title: 1. Interactive Streamlit Web UI
docs.text:
Run the programmatic serve command:

uv run grocery-helper serve

Or via Streamlit directly:

uv run streamlit run src/grocery_helper/app.py

Then open http://localhost:8501 in your browser.

docs.title: 2. Command-Line Interface (CLI)
docs.text:
To optimize a list directly in the terminal:

docs.title: ⌨️ Command-Line Interface (CLI) Reference
docs.text: The grocery-helper CLI allows automated, headless execution for shell scripts, scheduled tasks, and CI/CD pipelines.

docs.title: Subcommands Overview
docs.text: grocery-helper [-h] {serve,optimise} ...

docs.title: grocery-helper serve
docs.text:
Launch the Streamlit web application.

grocery-helper serve [--port PORT] [--host HOST]

docs.title: Options:
docs.text:
• --port PORT: Port to bind Streamlit server to (default: 8501).
  • --host HOST: Address to listen on (default: localhost).

docs.title: Example:
docs.text: grocery-helper serve --port 8080 --host 0.0.0.0

docs.title: grocery-helper optimise
docs.text:
Run the pricing optimizer for a grocery list.

grocery-helper optimise <list_id> [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Positional Arguments:
docs.text: • list_id: Identifier of the list to optimize (e.g. list_001).

docs.title: Options:
docs.text:
• --demo: Run in offline demo mode using built-in sample lists.
  • --zip ZIP: Specify store ZIP code for local pricing (default: from .env or 90210).
  • --max-stores N: Limit the shopping route to at most $N$ stores (e.g. 1 or 2).
  • --stores [STORES ...]: Space-separated list of store names to consider.
  • --json: Output raw JSON data instead of formatted terminal text.

docs.title: Basic Optimization in Demo Mode
docs.text: grocery-helper optimise list_001 --demo

docs.title: Restrict to at most 2 Stores
docs.text: grocery-helper optimise list_001 --demo --max-stores 2

docs.title: Compare Only ALDI and Trader Joe's
docs.text: grocery-helper optimise list_001 --demo --stores ALDI "Trader Joe's"

docs.title: Output JSON for Automation Scripts
docs.text:
grocery-helper optimise list_001 --demo --json

Sample JSON structure: 

{
  "list_id": "list_001",
  "list_name": "Weekly Shop",
  "store_assignments": {
    "item_001": "ALDI",
    "item_002": "ALDI",
    "item_005": "Kroger"
  },
  "total_cost": "23.140",
  "estimated_savings": "8.740",
  "single_store_totals": {
    "ALDI": "23.440",
    "Kroger": "26.370",
    "Trader Joe's": "26.680",
    "Whole Foods": "31.880"
  }
}

docs.title: 🖥️ Streamlit Web App Guide
docs.text: The Streamlit interface provides an interactive, visual dashboard for managing grocery lists and analyzing multi-store shopping routes.

docs.title: Launching the Web App
docs.text: uv run grocery-helper serve

docs.title: 1. Settings & Sidebar
docs.text:
• Credentials: Enter your AnyList email and password to sync your live account.
  • Store ZIP Code: Set your local ZIP code (e.g. 90210) to look up nearby grocers.
  • Demo Mode Toggle: When enabled, the app uses built-in sample lists and mock pricing.
  • Store Filters (Allowed Stores): Multiselect grocers to include or exclude (ALDI, Trader Joe's, Kroger, Whole Foods).
  • Max Stores Slider: Limit your route to at most $N$ stops (e.g. max_stores=1 for single-trip shopping).

docs.title: 2. In-App Item Management
docs.text: Above the results tabs, expand "➕ Add an Item to this List": - Enter an item name (e.g. "Greek Yogurt" or "Avocados"). - Specify quantity and unit (each, lb, oz, gallon, pack, liter). - Click "Add to List" to immediately update the list and re-calculate optimal pricing!

docs.title: 3. Price Comparison Tab
docs.text: A comprehensive data table detailing: - Every grocery item on your list and its quantity. - Prices across all considered stores (highlighting promotional sales). - The identified cheapest store and best unit price. - Potential savings compared to the highest-priced store.

docs.title: 4. Optimised Cart Tab
docs.text:
• Metric Cards:
  • Optimised Basket Total: Total cost when buying each item at its cheapest store.
  • Estimated Total Savings: Dollar amount saved across the basket.
  • Best Single Store: The cheapest single store if you only make one stop, along with the cost delta.
  • Cost Comparison Bar Chart: Visual comparison of the optimized split vs. shopping exclusively at ALDI, Kroger, Trader Joe's, or Whole Foods.
  • Store Route Expanders: Itemized shopping lists grouped by store with subtotals.
  • Export Store Lists to AnyList: A one-click button that creates store-specific sub-lists (e.g. "Weekly Shop (ALDI)") directly in your AnyList account.

docs.title: 🛍️ Shopper's Guide (Non-Developer)
docs.text: Welcome to Grocery Helper! This guide is written for everyday shoppers who want to save money on groceries without spending hours comparing store circulars or flipping between different shopping apps.

docs.title: 🎯 What Does Grocery Helper Do?
docs.text:
Grocery prices vary wildly between stores. Milk might be \$1.80 cheaper at ALDI, while fresh sourdough is cheaper at Trader Joe's, and your favorite coffee is on sale at Kroger.

Grocery Helper: 1. Connects to your AnyList grocery list (on your phone or computer). 2. Checks prices across nearby stores (ALDI, Trader Joe's, Kroger, and Whole Foods). 3. Tells you the cheapest single store to visit if you're in a hurry. 4. Tells you how much more you could save by splitting your trip between 2 or more stores. 5. Automatically creates store-specific shopping lists back on your phone so you can easily check items off while shopping!

flowchart LR
    A["📱 Your AnyList<br/>('Weekly Groceries')"] --> B["🛒 Grocery Helper<br/>(Price Comparison Engine)"]
    B --> C["🏪 Store A List<br/>('ALDI - Produce & Dairy')"]
    B --> D["🏪 Store B List<br/>('Trader Joe's - Snacks')"]

docs.title: 🚀 How to Start the App
docs.text:
You don't need to know how to code to run Grocery Helper.

  1. Open your computer's Terminal (Mac) or Command Prompt / PowerShell (Windows).
  2. Type or paste this command and press Enter: 
    grocery-helper serve
  3. Your web browser will automatically open with the Grocery Helper dashboard (at http://localhost:8501).

Closing the App

When you are done, simply close your browser window. In your terminal, you can press Ctrl + C to stop the app.

docs.title: 🧭 Step-by-Step Walkthrough
docs.text: When the web app opens, you'll see a clean shopping dashboard with a sidebar on the left and your shopping lists on the right.

docs.title: Step 1: Choose Demo Mode or Connect Your AnyList Account
docs.text:
• Just Want to Try It Out? Keep Demo Mode checked in the left sidebar! The app comes preloaded with sample lists ("Weekly Shop", "Party Supplies", and "Brunch & Coffee") so you can test all features without entering any credentials.
  • Ready to Use Your Own Lists? In the left sidebar, uncheck Demo Mode and enter your AnyList Email and Password. Your lists will automatically appear in the dropdown menu.

[!NOTE] Your AnyList password is stored only on your computer in your local configuration and is never sent to third-party tracking servers.

docs.title: Step 2: Choose Your Local Stores
docs.text:
Not everyone has every grocery store nearby. In the sidebar under "Allowed Stores": - Check the stores you are willing to shop at (e.g., ALDI, Trader Joe's, Kroger). - Uncheck any stores that aren't near you or that you don't prefer.

You can also enter your ZIP Code to automatically find the closest branch locations.

docs.title: Step 3: Choose Your Trip Style ("Max Stores" Slider)
docs.text:
How much time do you have to shop this week? Use the "Max Store Stops" slider to set your preference:

Slider Setting What It Means Best For 1 Store Finds the single cheapest store for your entire basket. Zero extra driving. Busy weekdays or quick errands. 2 Stores Splits your basket across the top 2 stores to unlock major savings while keeping driving manageable. The sweet spot for weekly shopping! 3+ Stores Finds the absolute rock-bottom price across every store. Maximum possible budget savings.

docs.title: Step 4: Review Your Savings & Price Comparisons
docs.text: Click the Price Comparison tab to see a breakdown of your list: - Each item is shown alongside its price at every selected store. - Green badges highlight promotional sales and discounts. - The Cheapest Store column shows you exactly where to buy each item. - The Savings column shows how much you save on each product compared to the highest-priced store.

docs.title: Step 5: Add Extra or Forgotten Items
docs.text:
Realized you forgot something while reviewing prices? 1. Click the "➕ Add an Item to this List" box above the tabs. 2. Type in the item name (e.g. "Greek Yogurt" or "Honeycrisp Apples"). 3. Choose the quantity and unit (e.g. 2, lb). 4. Click "Add to List".

The app immediately refreshes with the updated totals and savings!

docs.title: Step 6: Export Custom Lists to Your Phone
docs.text:
Once you're happy with your shopping plan, switch to the Optimised Cart tab: 1. Review your total spend, your estimated savings, and the items assigned to each store. 2. Click the big green button: "📤 Export Store Lists to AnyList". 3. Open the AnyList app on your iPhone or Android.

You will find new, beautifully organized sub-lists (for example, "Weekly Groceries (ALDI)" and "Weekly Groceries (Trader Joe's)"). When you walk into ALDI, open your ALDI list and check off items as you go!

docs.title: 📝 Tips for Writing Items in AnyList
docs.text: Grocery Helper includes a smart matching engine that automatically detects item sizes, units, and spelling. Follow these simple tips when adding items to your grocery list for the most accurate prices:

docs.title: Include Quantities and Units
docs.text: If you know how much you need, include the quantity right in the item title: - "Honeycrisp Apples 3 lbs" - "Whole Milk 1 gal" - "Diet Coke 12pk" - "Eggs 1 dozen" (or "Eggs 12ct")

docs.title: Specify Varieties or Organic
docs.text: If you prefer organic or specific varieties, mention it: - "Organic Bananas" vs. "Bananas" - "Sourdough Bread" vs. "Bread" - "Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast" vs. "Chicken"

docs.title: Don't Worry About Minor Typos
docs.text: The matching engine automatically corrects minor spelling differences (e.g., "avacados", "spinich" or abbreviations like "Coffee w/ milk").

docs.title: Do I need a paid AnyList subscription?
docs.text: No. Grocery Helper works with both free AnyList accounts and AnyList Complete (paid) accounts.

docs.title: What if I don't have an AnyList account?
docs.text: You can still use Grocery Helper completely free in Demo Mode! It will give you realistic price comparisons, route optimizations, and savings estimates using built-in grocery lists.

docs.title: How does Grocery Helper know grocery prices?
docs.text:
• Live Store APIs: For supported chains like Kroger (and its family of stores like Ralphs, Dillons, King Soopers, Fred Meyer), Grocery Helper connects directly to live product catalogs and weekly sale circulars.
  • Regional Price Models: For chains like ALDI and Trader Joe's, Grocery Helper uses calibrated regional grocery price benchmarks that reflect everyday retail pricing.

docs.title: What if a store doesn't carry an item on my list?
docs.text: If an item isn't available at a specific store, Grocery Helper flags it and automatically assigns that item to another store on your route that does carry it.

docs.title: Can I run this without an internet connection?
docs.text: Yes! In Demo Mode, Grocery Helper works 100% offline without needing an active internet connection.
